Methods of Chemical Analysis of Ferrous Metals Sectional Committee, MTD 2

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis of Ferrous Metals Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. Ferro-silicon-zirconium alloys are master alloys which are required for making additions of silicon and especially zirconium to prepare iron base alloys. Zirconium is for refinement and grain size improvement and silicon for impart ing strength to the alloys. In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'.

Acid, 48 percent.

5.3.1 Zron/lVickef Crucible, 30 ml capacity. 5.3.2 PTFE Beakers, 250 ml capcity. 5.3.3 Platinum Crucible, 30 ml capacity. 5.4 Procedure 5.4.1 Transfer 0.5 g of the sample to a 30 ml iron/ nickel (preferable) crucible. Add 5 g of sodium peroxide. Mix thoroughly using an iron/rtickel platinum rod and transfer any adhering particles on the rod to the crucible by gently tapping. 5.4.2 Cover the mixture with a layer of 2 g sodium peroxide. Heat the crucible on a hot plate for 10-15 min to expel any moisture. Carefilly fuse over a low flame muffle furnace, slowly rotating the crucible, until the contents have melted. Increase the temperature to bright redness for a minute. 5.4.3 Remove the crucible from the flame, cover and allow to cool. Tap the crucible gently and transfer it to a 250 ml stainless steel PTFE beaker. Add 50 ml water cautiously.When the reaction ceases, remove the crucible and rinse with water, adding the washings to the beaker. 5.4.4 Acidi& with hydrochloric acid (1:1), add another 50 ml hydrochloric acid (1:1). Transfer the solution to a 250 ml glass beaker. Wash the stainless steel/PTFE beaker with hydrochloric acid (1: 1), transferring the washings to the glass beaker. 5.4.5 Evaporate to dryness on a water bath when the residue is dry, allow to-cool. Add 20 ml hydrochloric acid, stir well cover the beaker, and heat for a few minutes. Dilute with 200 ml of hot water, digest for a few minutes and filter through a filter paper, containing some filter pulp. Wash with hot hydrochloric acid (5 : 95) eight times and then thoroughly with hot water. Reserve the paper and residue.

3 SAMPLING The sample shall be drawn and prepared as per the method given in IS 1472. 4 QUALITY OF REAGENTS Unless specified otherwise, analytical grade reagents and distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be employed for the test. 5 DETERMINATION OF SILICON GRAVIMETRIC METHOD 5.1 Outline of the Method The sample is decomposed by fusion with sodium peroxide. Silica is separated by dehydration with hydrochloric acid. The solution is filtered. Silica is ignited and weighed. It is then volatilized with hydrofluoric acid. The residue is ignited and weighed. The loss in mass represent silica. BY THE

IS 15396:2003 5.4.6 Evaporate the filtrate to dryness and bake to 11O('C for 1 h. Cool, add 20 ml hydrochloric acid, digest on a water bath for 10 min. Add 20 ml water, stir well, filter and wash with hot hydrochloric acid (5:95) eight times and then with hot water, till free from chloride. Preserve the filtrate, after making it up to 250 ml. 5.4.7 Place the filter paper with residue in a 50 ml platinum crucible, heat slowly to remove, the water, raise the heat to char the paper and finally ignite at 1 IOO"C, after covering the crucible. Cool in a desiccator. Weigh and again ignite at 11O"Cfor 10 min and check for constancy in mass. Add 2 to 3 ml sulphuric acid (1:1) to moisten the residue, followed by 5 ml hydrofluoric acid. Evaporate to dryness, ignite at 1 100"C and weigh. 5.5 Blank Carry out a blank determination procedure, but without the sample. 5.6 Calculation Silicon, percent by mass where

6.3.1 Pipette out an aliquot, containing approximately 50 to 100 mg iron, from the solution preserved10 under 5.4.6 and transfer to a 600 ml beaker. Add stannous chloride solution, dropwise till the yellow colour of the solution disappears. Add 3 drops in excess. Dilute to 200 ml with water and cool to 10"C. Add 15 ml of saturated mercuric chloride solution, all at once. Mix well and keep on the water bath for 3 to 5 min. 6.3.2 Add 20 ml of acid mixture and 5 drops of indicator solution. Dilute to 400 ml and titrate with standard potassium bichromate solution to a distinct purple end point. 6.3.3 Blank Determine the blank value of the reagents, using the same amount of all reagents and following the procedure. Before titration with potassium bichromate solution, add 1.0 ml of ferrous ammonium -sulphate solution. In another beaker, place 400 ml of cold dilute sulphuric acid and add 1 ml of ferrous ammonium sulphate solution. Add 20 ml of acid mixture and 5 drops of indicator. Titrate with potassium bichromate solution. Record this titration and substract the value obtained from the bIank, to get the corrected blank. 6.4 Calculation Iron, percentbymass=

7.3.3 Dissolve the precipitate on the filter using 30 ml ammonia (1:4) and collect the solution in the same beaker in which precipitation was carried out. Repeat this operation twice, using each time, 30 ml ammonia (1:4). Finally give 2 washings to the filter paper with 5 ml of ammonia (1:9). See that the ammonia solution comes in contact with all sides of the beaker and that any adhering precipitate is brought into solution. 7.3.4 .Add 25 ml mandelic acid solution, 3 drops of methyl.red indicator, and neutralize with hydrochloric acid. Add 10 ml of hydrochloric acid, in excess, stir and allow to digest on the water bath for I h. 7.3.5 Filter warm, through a close textured filter paper and wash the precipitate six times with 1.0 ml of 10 percent cold mandelic acid wash solution. 7.3.6 Transfer the paper and precipitate to a tared platinum crucible, dry, char and finally heat to.1 OOO�C. Keep at this temperature for 30 min.
